newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower on profit taking.

text.p: Stocks closed lower on Saturday after two days of rises due to late profit taking, brokers said.
"Profit taking emerged toward the close as fears of an oversupply of stocks this month chilled sentiment," said Choo Hee-yup, a broker at Dongwon Securities.
The composite stock index ended 2.14 points lower at a provisional 765.73.
Choo said rights and bonus issues in November were estimated at 650 billion won. State-backed Korea Telecom will also sell 13.3 million shares this month, valued at 500 billion won.
Brokers said the market rose in early trading, backed by the government's announcement on Friday of a plan to delay privatisation of four big state-run corporations.
The finance ministry said it would be difficult to sell a large amount of government stock due to the current depression of the stock market.
Volume totalled 21.53 million shares for Saturday's half-day trading, compared with 29.18 million on Friday.
Gainers outpaced losers 433 to 413 with 154 unchanged.
